title: Returning seconds breaks fetchWithTimeout, which feeds the result to AbortSignal.timeout (milliseconds)
rationale: src/http.ts line 8 passes parseDuration's result straight to AbortSignal.timeout, which interprets its argument in milliseconds and was not updated by this change. A configured "30s" timeout now aborts after 30 ms and "1500ms" waits 1.5 s, so requests through fetchWithTimeout fail or run with a timeout 1000x off; the same applies to the "m" branch on line 15 and the "ms" branch on line 11.

title: Lookup no longer returns ErrNotFound, breaking the documented sentinel contract
rationale: The package documents that Lookup returns ErrNotFound when the id is absent, but the error is no longer wrapped in the sentinel, so callers matching via errors.Is or == will treat a missing user as a real failure. Returning fmt.Errorf("user %q: %w", id, ErrNotFound) preserves the contract while adding the id.

title: Lookup no longer returns ErrNotFound, breaking errors.Is callers
rationale: Lookup previously returned the sentinel ErrNotFound, and web/users.go:17 still relies on errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) to map a missing user to 404. The new fmt.Errorf result does not wrap ErrNotFound, so the check fails and every not-found request is reported as a 500 Internal Server Error.

title: Negative limit bypasses the MAX_PAGE guard and pulls the whole table
rationale: The guard only rejects limit > MAX_PAGE, but SQLite treats a negative LIMIT as no limit, so fetch_orders(conn, 0, -1) returns every row — exactly the whole-table pull the new docstring claims is prevented. A caller using the common negative-limit-as-unbounded convention silently bypasses the check.

title: Remaining() now returns megabytes, silently changing the unit of a byte-based exported API
rationale: Quota is a byte-accounting type (New takes a byte limit, Record charges bytes), and Remaining() previously returned bytes; it now returns whole megabytes while keeping its name. Any caller that treats the result as bytes — for admission checks like uploadSize <= Remaining() or for byte display — is off by a factor of 2^20, and the type system gives no signal. The dashboard's need is better met by a separate megabyte method or converting at the dashboard call site, leaving Remaining() in bytes.

title: Lookup no longer returns ErrNotFound, breaking its documented contract
rationale: The documented contract — ErrNotFound is returned when no user has the id — is broken: Lookup returns a wrapped fmt.Errorf that fails any errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) check, so callers matching on ErrNotFound treat a missing user as an unexpected error. Wrapping with %w as suggested restores the contract.

title: Existing export caller now raises ValueError on every call
rationale: app/export.py sets BATCH = 500 and calls fetch_orders(conn, offset, BATCH) in a loop, so on the first iteration limit=500 exceeds MAX_PAGE=100 and export_orders raises ValueError instead of exporting anything. Every existing caller of export_orders now fails at runtime.

title: Exported parseDuration now returns seconds instead of milliseconds, with no caller updates in this change
rationale: The return value changes by a factor of 1000 for every input, and this diff updates no call sites. The consequence rests on callers not shown in this diff consuming the old millisecond value or compensating with their own division by 1000; the new doc comment's reference to a config consumer suggests such a caller may exist, but its expectations are not demonstrated. Existing call sites need to be audited and updated in the same change, or the unit change confirmed safe.

title: Remaining silently changes its return unit from bytes to megabytes for every caller
rationale: Remaining previously returned bytes while Record on the same type still charges bytes, so any caller other than the dashboard that consumed the value as bytes — for example admission control comparing an upload size against remaining quota — now silently receives a number 2^20 times smaller, with no type-level signal since the signature is unchanged. Converting to megabytes at the dashboard call site, or adding a distinctly named method, would preserve the byte contract for the package's other callers.

title: Existing caller export_orders now raises ValueError on every call
rationale: app/export.py defines BATCH = 500 and calls fetch_orders(conn, offset, BATCH) in a loop, so the new page-size cap makes export_orders raise ValueError on its first iteration. CSV export is broken entirely; the cap was added without checking the existing caller's page size.

title: Remaining() now returns megabytes, but web/upload.go still compares it against a byte count
rationale: internal/web/upload.go:22 compares Remaining() against int64(len(body)) in bytes. With the new megabyte definition, a 1 GB limit with nothing used yields Remaining() == 1024, so any body over 1024 bytes is rejected with 413 — every legitimate upload fails. Keep Remaining() in bytes and expose the whole-megabyte figure under a separate method for the dashboard.

title: Lookup no longer returns ErrNotFound, breaking the documented contract and its caller
rationale: The documented ErrNotFound sentinel is replaced by a fmt.Errorf without %w, so errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) in web/users.go line 17 no longer matches and requests for missing users return 500 instead of 404. Wrap with fmt.Errorf("user %q: %w", id, ErrNotFound) to preserve the sentinel.

title: Unit change to seconds breaks the existing caller, which passes the result to AbortSignal.timeout (milliseconds)
rationale: src/http.ts calls AbortSignal.timeout(parseDuration(timeout)), which takes milliseconds; with the new seconds semantics a configured "30s" timeout becomes 30 ms and "1500ms" becomes 1.5 ms, so every request through fetchWithTimeout aborts essentially immediately. The function's only shown caller still assumes the old millisecond contract, so the change guarantees wrong behavior on a reachable path.

title: Remaining() now returns whole megabytes, but the upload handler compares it against a byte count, rejecting nearly all uploads
rationale: web/upload.go line 22 evaluates h.Quota.Remaining() < int64(len(body)), so the megabyte figure is compared against a byte length: with 64 MB of quota remaining, Remaining() returns 64 and any body larger than 64 bytes is rejected with 413, so the upload endpoint fails for essentially every real request. The enforcement path needs Remaining() to stay in bytes; the dashboard's whole-MB figure needs a separate accessor, which spans the dashboard code not shown here.
